book.title: Hold Me Tight: Seven Conversations for a Lifetime of Love
book.author: Sue Johnson

confidence_note: Book text not read; the three dialogues are consistent across several secondary pages. Omitted: invented woman-pursues/man-withdraws case with quotes, unattributed 80 percent figure, gender roles. Goodreads' 'fourth category' ignored as a summary error.
facts: First of seven conversations: recognising the demon dialogues; tracking the conflict pattern (which Johnson's popular literature calls a 'dance') is a hallmark of stage one.
Find the Bad Guy: partners go in a circle blaming each other, self-protection, deadlock; partners expecting it react faster.
Protest Polka: one partner reaches out and protests the disconnect; the other withdraws and pushes against perceived criticism; image of knocking on a brick wall.
Freeze and Flee: follows the polka; pursuer has given up, both step back; icy silence, no connection positive or negative; both protect themselves from rejection and contempt.
Suggested response: treat the pattern as a shared enemy, stay in the present, recognise each other's desperation; the connection may be 'forgotten' not gone.

In the nine-step model the more withdrawn partner is usually invited to go through the steps slightly ahead; stage one identifies the issues and cycle, accesses attachment emotions and reframes the problem as the cycle.
tension: Each partner's self-protection feeds the other's.
opening_idea: Open on the icy silence or the circle of blame.

lessons.idea: Name the loop out loud and treat the pattern as the opponent.

reflect_final: Which of the three patterns is closest to a loop you recognise in your own life?

use_cases.situation: Colleagues fall into the same argument
use_cases.move: Name the loop before the issue.

use_cases.situation: Teen and parent end talks with a slammed door
use_cases.move: Pause and treat the argument as the shared problem.
Recognise Find the Bad Guy and say what you want.
